newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to defy U.S. over no-fly zones - papers.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to defy U.S. over no-fly zones - papers.

text.p: Iraq's official newspapers, including Babel of President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, reiterated on Wednesday that Baghdad would ignore Western restrictions on flights by Iraqi aircraft.

"Once again we say to the ungodly Americans in a loud voice...(that) from today there are no more imaginary parallel lines...from today there will be no (part) of Iraqi territory off limits to us whether in the north or the south," Babel said in a front-page editorial.
"We shall defend our sovereignty with our nails and teeth," Babel said.
The official al-Qadissiya newspaper said Iraq's decision not to accept no-fly zones over its territory was irrevocable.
" Iraq has obliterated for ever the damned lines north of the 36th parallel and south of the 32nd parallel."

The U.S. decided on Tuesday to extend the air-exclusion zone in southern Iraq to the 33rd parallel and Saddam on Tuesday declared Western no-fly zones in both the southern and northern parts of Iraq null and void.
He urged his pilots and anti-aircraft gunners to shoot down any Western plane entering those zones.

The U.S. fired cruise missiles at Iraqi air defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday. The attacks were prompted by Saturday's incursion by Iraqi armed forces into Kurdish areas in northern Iraq.
The newspapers also hit out at President Bill Clinton and one described him as "a dinosaur" trying to swallow the world with his computerised weapons systems.
"Let the cursed Clinton be humiliated. The roar of Iraqis will not let him sleeep at night," said Qadissiya.
